evals.prompt: I have a Django project at ~/work/fresh-shop with DRF endpoints for products and orders. Can you set up admineverywhere on it? I want the admin to be called "Fresh Shop" and use our logo at static/img/fresh-logo.svg.
evals.expected_output: Runs inspect_project.py on ~/work/fresh-shop, checks DRF/spectacular/authtoken prerequisites, installs the plugin (pip install admineverywhere or -e), edits settings.py (INSTALLED_APPS + ADMINEVERYWHERE_BRAND_DIR) and urls.py (include admineverywhere.urls) with the user's confirmation, runs derive_brand.py with --name 'Fresh Shop' --logo static/img/fresh-logo.svg, points app/public/config.json at the API, and verifies with curl (schema, token route, branding 404). Reports a table of every edit with file:line and the run commands.

evals.prompt: onboard this repo onto admineverywhere, don't ask me anything, just make it work. repo is at /srv/api — it's a Django REST thing my colleague wrote
evals.expected_output: Chooses AUTO mode explicitly. Scans with inspect_project.py; if DRF or drf-spectacular or token auth is missing, installs and wires them (proposing exact diffs but proceeding per 'don't ask'), wires admineverywhere into settings/urls, derives the brand automatically (name from pyproject/README — NOT 'backend'/'api' generics; generated grid icons if no logo), verifies the chain with curl, and reports everything applied plus anything left for the user (superuser, prod CORS).

evals.prompt: Add an admin app to my Django REST Framework API — I heard admineverywhere renders the whole CRUD from the OpenAPI schema. What do I need to change in my project?
evals.expected_output: Triggers the skill; explains the three prerequisites (rest_framework, drf-spectacular served publicly, token auth route), runs the inspection, and gives the exact settings.py/urls.py diff + pip install line. Does not hardcode any product name; mentions the branding step and asks (ASK mode) for name/palette/logo preferences in one batch before applying.
